summary.text: 渴 combines a water-related element with a sound element. Its common meanings are “thirsty” and “parched”; an older use means “exhausted” or “dried up.”

formation.text: 渴 is a phonosemantic compound: 氵 marks a water-related meaning category, while 曷 is analyzed as its sound element. An early dictionary glosses the character as “exhausted”; that analysis records an early interpretation, not proof of the graph’s prehistoric origin.

components.text: 氵 contributes the water-related meaning category in 渴. The cited analysis does not establish a separate historical form relationship for this shape.
曷 is analyzed as the sound element in 渴. The ancient referent of part of 曷’s bronze form is uncertain; this does not rule out its sound role here.

sound_limitation.text: The reconstructions differ in important details, and the sound comparison alone does not establish 曷’s role in 渴.

sound.text: These forms share rhyme and coda material but have different initials in this reconstruction, so the comparison is qualified.
This reconstruction gives different alternatives for 渴; the comparison therefore remains qualified.
The present-day Mandarin readings differ; this pair does not establish their ancient sound relation.

history.text: The cited account presents bronze, seal, and manuscript examples and analyzes a bronze form as 水 plus phonetic 曷. These examples do not provide a complete dated sequence.

A bronze use of 渴 for 竭 is reported in connection with the Zhongshan King Fanghu inscription, as is a Mawangdui Laozi manuscript use. The available Fanghu transcription prints 竭, so it does not independently confirm the precise graph.
An early dictionary analyzes 渴 as 从水、曷聲 and glosses it as “exhausted.” This is an early lexicographic analysis, not direct evidence of the graph’s earliest formation.

uncertainties.text: The cited analysis does not securely identify the original referent of the middle element in 曷’s bronze form. This uncertainty does not by itself rule out 曷’s phonetic role in 渴.
The bronze analysis describes 水, while the modern graph has 氵. The cited material does not trace the graphic development between them.

senses.text: A bronze use is interpreted as “drying up” or “exhausted,” with the graph reported as writing 竭. The Fanghu transcription itself prints 竭 and does not independently confirm the graph identification.

senses.period: Cited in 詩·王風·君子于役; earliest physical witness date unresolved
senses.text: A cited Shijing passage uses 渴 to mean “thirsty.” The date of the passage’s earliest surviving physical witness is unresolved.
A cited Tang usage has the sense “dry” or “parched.”
A cited 公羊傳 passage uses 渴 to mean “urgent”; its relation to the other senses is not established.

developments.text: A shift from “exhausted” or “dried up” to “thirsty” is plausible, but the intervening stages are not traced.

limitations.text: The bronze use is reported with the meaning “exhausted” or “dried up,” but is not securely established as the character’s original meaning. The earliest physical witness for the cited thirst passage is also unresolved.
The separate sense “urgent” is recorded, but its development or connection to the other senses is not established.
